cvEn:
Ben Zion Amarant, son of Hana and Avraham, was born on 25 Cheshvan 5706 (1 November 1945) at Kibbutz Mizra. He studied at the educational institution there, and afterwards at the ORT school in Afula, where he completed his studies. About four years before his death, his parents took him to the United States for surgery on his heart, and his main concern was whether he would be found fit to serve in the IDF. His joy was great when the time came and he was accepted into the Air Force (in August 1963), even though the medical committee advised him to forgo his military service obligation.

He studied at the Air Force technical school, and took pride in his military uniform. He made many friends among his commanders and fellow recruits through the precious qualities of his character and, above all, through his modesty. He took a course for jet mechanics and linked these studies to his plans to continue working as a mechanic on the kibbutz. He fell while performing his duties on 17 Tevet 5724 (2 January 1964), and was laid to rest in the civilian cemetery at Kibbutz Mizra. During the shiva for him, a special issue of "Dapei Mizra" (the kibbutz's internal newsletter) appeared, devoted entirely to his memory. On the first anniversary of his death, Kibbutz Mizra published a memorial booklet. On the same occasion, a library was established in his memory for the students of the ORT school in Afula, bearing his name.
